description: Compute a bounded complex radix-two DFT and four exact fixed-field operations: polynomial multiplication, disjoint-subset convolution, affine linear-system solution and least discrete logarithm. Complex f64 and field-residue outputs are separate semantic types.
forward: Compute a bounded complex radix-two DFT and four exact fixed-field operations: polynomial multiplication, disjoint-subset convolution, affine linear-system solution and least discrete logarithm. Complex f64 and field-residue outputs are separate semantic types.

Each leaf is std-only; no production calls among these modules. Zero-padded FFT convolution may be compared with Karatsuba only on small representable integer fixtures with explicit rounding/error checks. Fixed-field subset convolution with invertible empty coefficient yields a triangular field system solvable by Gaussian elimination only when the2^d unknowns fit128. BSGS output can be checked by modular powering under the same fixed modulus.
inverse: Exclude wrong modular product coefficients, overlapping-subset terms, noncanonical residues, invalid affine particular/nullspace certificates or a nonleast/incorrect discrete exponent. For FFT exclude wrong length, nonfinite output, wrong phase/normalization or wrong native butterfly result; do not impose exact complex-theory equalities on rounded values. Exclude replacing field residues with raw floating magnitudes or equating resource refusal with algebraic None.

Ideal fixed-size DFT is invertible; rounded FFT can merge input bit patterns. Polynomial product admits factor scaling(a*c,b/c) and zero-product ambiguity. Subset output with fixed a and a[empty]!=0 uniquely recovers b in the field, while zero a admits every b. Gaussian output admits many row-equivalent systems. BSGS Some0 admits every base with target1, and modular normalization makes raw representatives nonunique.
limitations: FFT inverse identities and convolution theorem are real/complex target identities, not universal f64 error bounds or an isomorphism to a finite field. Modular algebra is exact inside fixed prime; no caller-supplied composite modulus is supported. Allocator exhaustion follows std policy. No callbacks or executable percentage profiles.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
